videos.script:
Some controls are hard to build well. A dialog has to take the focus, keep it, hide the page behind it from a screen reader, and give the focus back. This lesson borrows those from a library instead of building them.

{{adding}} You add Angular Material at an exact version, and look at everything it changed. One of those changes asks Google for a font on every visit, and you undo it.

{{components}} The session's checkbox becomes a Material checkbox, and a screen reader hears the same box as before.

{{cdk}} Under Material sits the CDK: behaviour without a look.

{{dialog}} Lesson eighteen's confirm becomes a Material dialog that traps the focus and returns it.

{{announce}} The live announcer tells a screen reader that sessions were added.

{{cost}} And the build says what all of it weighs, and where.
